# Rambling

- saw Travis Gerke's [Quack to the Future](https://tgerke.github.io/quack-to-the-future/) talk at posit::conf 2026 — {ducklake} + {dplyneage}
- [dplyneage](https://tgerke.github.io/dplyneage/) draws column-level lineage for dplyr pipelines as a React Flow diagram
- question: can this run fully in the browser via webR? no install, editable demo
- open questions
    -  does dplynesage wokr on duckdplyr/dcklack wiht any database not jsut ducdkdb?
    - what is simulati_posgres(); why not sim_duckdb or soemthing?

# Simple Reprex

Runs in your browser with webR — no R install. Edit the pipeline and hit **Run Code**; the first run downloads packages, so give it a moment.

```{webr}
library(dplyr); library(dbplyr); library(dplyneage)

lin <- lazy_frame(id = 1, amt = 2, con = simulate_postgres()) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(total = sum(amt, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  extract_lineage()

lin
lineage_flow(lin)
```
